newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper bids to strip court's power.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper bids to strip court's power.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper has drafted legislation that would strip Colombia's Constitutional Court of the power to determine when a president is able to rule by decree, government sources said on Tuesday.

They said the bill, which would give Samper virtual dictatorial powers, was drawn up after last week's vote by the court overturning the government's three-month-old state of economic emergency on the grounds it was unconstitutional.

Government finances were left in disarray by the court ruling last Wednesday. Samper, dogged by allegations that he used drug money to finance his presidential campaign, said he had no doubt that it was politically motivated.

If the legislation is approved by Congress, dominated by Samper's Liberal Party, the president would be granted sweeping powers to declare emergency rule and ram through measures -- including economic austerity plans -- without the prior approval of Congress.

Under the current system of checks and balances, the Constitutional Court is the final arbiter of when the executive branch is legitimately empowered to declare a state of emergency and rule by decree.

Sources in the Casa de Narino presidential palace said the bill aimed at taking that power away from the court would be presented to Congress by Interior Minister Horacio Serpa as early as Tuesday afternoon.
Serpa, Samper's right-hand man and a likely candidate to succeed him in elections next year, could not be reached for immediate comment.
